records.summary: This would provide MV3 replacements for Edge and Chrome extensions whose developers have not migrated them. The idea was to sell those replacements through a small Pro tier.
records.customer: Users of orphaned Edge and Chrome extensions
records.market: Microsoft Edge Add-ons and Chrome Web Store

competitors.name: Microsoft Purview
competitors.note: Named as an example of a large orphaned extension that belongs to a vendor.

competitors.name: Cisco Webex
competitors.note: Named as an example of a large orphaned extension that belongs to a vendor.

competitors.name: HP Dynamic Audio
competitors.note: Named as an example of a large orphaned extension that belongs to a vendor.

competitors.name: bank Ukey extensions
competitors.note: Named as examples of large orphaned extensions that belong to vendors.

rounds.plain: Popular extensions had already migrated or belonged to vendors, while the long-tail orphans were judged too small to pay. The report found no evidence that users would pay and no moat.

risks: The migration window closes as Edge switch-off completes at the end of 2026.
A third party cannot replace vendor-owned extensions.
No evidence that orphaned-extension users pay.
records.moat: None; extensions can be ported by anyone, and first-mover listing or SEO was the only proposed edge.

records.summary: This would be an iOS-first companion app for checking Premium Bonds prizes. The scout proposed it as an alternative to NS&I’s checker, with Android already having a third-party app.
records.customer: UK Premium Bonds holders
records.market: GB; Apple App Store and Google Play

competitors.name: NS&I Premium Bonds prize checker
competitors.note: Official checker; 2.6★ from 1.4k ratings on iOS.

competitors.name: NS&I mobile app
competitors.note: Shows Premium Bonds prize history and sends prize notifications by text and email.

competitors.name: Premium Bonds Prize Checker +
competitors.note: Third-party Android checker; scout reports 4.1★ and 10k+ downloads.

competitors.name: Numo
competitors.note: Named in the scout as an iOS entrant with 0 ratings.

rounds.plain: The official channel already covers the job, winning-number data is free, and the reports found no evidence that people pay for a checker. The report also flags trademark and App Store review risk.

risks: “Premium Bonds” and NS&I are NS&I marks, creating App Store review and trademark risk.
Free data makes the app easy to copy.
No evidence of willingness to pay.
records.moat: Low; the data is free and the app is trivial to clone.

records.summary: This would be an Octopus Energy smart-tariff companion with widgets and alerts for the cheapest usage slots. It was framed as a successor to OctoTracker for its existing users.
records.customer: Octopus Energy customers using smart tariffs
records.market: Apple App Store and Google Play

competitors.name: OctoTracker
competitors.note: Existing tracker; its iOS app was last updated 25 Jun 2025, and the report says it moved to a web app, though the developer match was unverified.

competitors.name: Octopus Compare
competitors.note: Dropped its app for a web version.

rounds.plain: The report found no moat: the Octopus API is free and public, competing apps are active, and Octopus’s own app shows tariff prices. Two incumbents moving from apps to the web was taken as a sign that the apps may not pay.

risks: The idea depends on a public API and on Octopus not absorbing the features.
Active competitors already exist.
The reports suggest app economics may be weak.
records.moat: None identified; the API is free and public, and the features are easy to copy.

records.summary: This would connect FreeAgent to e-commerce and payment services, including posting settlements, and add missing automation actions such as invoice creation. The scout focused on users left without FreeAgent’s discontinued Shopify integration or the desired Zapier actions.
records.customer: FreeAgent users needing e-commerce settlement posting or more automation actions
records.market: FreeAgent ecosystem, Shopify App Store, Zapier
records.paid_demand: Paid entrants are named in the reports: Equali is listed at $23-47/mo in the scout, and FreeAgent users get 20% off. The reports do not verify their revenue.

competitors.name: Equali
competitors.note: Officially listed by FreeAgent; covers Shopify, Amazon, eBay and Etsy.

competitors.name: A2X
competitors.note: Report says it does not support FreeAgent.

competitors.name: Link My Books
competitors.note: Report says it does not support FreeAgent.

competitors.name: Synder
competitors.note: Report says it does not support FreeAgent.

rounds.plain: The gap exists, but Equali has FreeAgent’s official listing and discount, giving it a distribution edge. The report says it would reopen the idea if Equali falters and FreeAgent agrees to list a second partner.

risks: Equali has an official distribution advantage.
Accounting correctness brings support load and liability.
The rule flags possible support above 5 h/week.
records.moat: Equali has an official listing and discount; accounting correctness may create a barrier but also adds support and liability.
records.next_steps: Watch for Equali to falter and whether FreeAgent agrees to list a second partner.

records.summary: This would replace Google Chat notifications for Jira Cloud with an app addressing setup and notification complaints about the incumbent. The scout proposed a replacement for an app that had not been updated since 2021.
records.customer: Jira Cloud teams using Google Chat notifications
records.paid_demand: The incumbent has 11,005 installs, but the reports provide no evidence that users pay for a replacement. A paid Forge competitor is listed, though its install count is not shown.

competitors.name: Google LLC’s Google Chat for Jira Cloud
competitors.note: Incumbent with 11,005 installs and 2.30★ from 110 reviews; last release 11 Nov 2021.

competitors.name: Canary Apps Google Chat for Jira
Canary Apps Google Chat Automation Actions for Jira
Chatpane
competitors.note: Forge app released 16 Oct 2026; pitch addresses complaints about setup and threading.

competitors.name: Jira Automation
competitors.note: Its “Send web request” can post to a Chat webhook.

rounds.plain: A new entrant already targets the same complaints, and a competent free alternative exists. The report also says Google could fix its own app at any time and the extra-hard moat check fails.

risks: Paid competition would face free alternatives.
Google could update its own app.
Forge apps are cheap to copy.
records.moat: Weak; a Forge app is cheap to copy, and competing apps already exist.

records.summary: This would replace the stale official Harvest time-tracking integration for Jira Cloud. The scout highlighted complaints about integration with Jira time-tracking fields and recording time against tickets on other dates.
records.customer: Jira Cloud teams using Harvest for time tracking

competitors.name: Harvest Time Tracking (Official)
competitors.note: 2,439 installs, 2.53★ from 145 ratings; last release 29 Jun 2021.

rounds.plain: The report found nine apps for “harvest,” including several alternatives to the official app. The market was judged to fail the moat check.

risks: Several competitors are already listed.
The official app has a small install base compared with the proposed opportunity.
records.moat: Fails the moat check; multiple alternatives exist, including several small apps.

records.summary: This is a general strategy of replacing official Atlassian integrations whose vendors have shut down or stopped updating them. The scout examined stale apps with at least 1,000 installs as potential openings.
records.customer: Atlassian Marketplace users of abandoned or stale integrations

competitors.name: InVision & Freehand+ replacement apps
competitors.note: Two replacement apps were released 22 Oct 2026 after InVision shut down.

competitors.name: Chatpane
competitors.note: Fresh competitor for the Google Chat orphan, built around its complaints.

rounds.plain: The report found that orphan events attract replacements quickly, while the Forge revenue-share terms make cloning cheap. It says only orphans with no named successor and more than 5k installs might merit consideration.

risks: Replacement apps can appear quickly after an orphan event.
Forge apps are cheap to clone.
records.moat: Weak; copying speed is high and new competitors have appeared quickly in examples reviewed.

records.summary: This would be a better Mermaid diagram app for Confluence Cloud. The scout was prompted by weak ratings for two leading apps.
records.customer: Confluence Cloud users who need Mermaid diagrams

rounds.plain: The report found 107 apps matching “mermaid,” including several actively updated and rated 4.0–4.6★. It judged the market crowded.

risks: Many competing apps already exist.
records.moat: No moat identified; the report found 107 matching apps, several actively maintained.

records.summary: This would provide a third-party fix for problems users report with Stripe and PayPal payment feeds into Xero. The scout focused on complaints about fees and Xero’s account-creation flow.
records.customer: Xero users connecting Stripe or PayPal

competitors.name: Stripe
competitors.note: First-party/payment-provider app; complaints described in the report target Stripe or Xero.

competitors.name: PayPal
competitors.note: Payment-provider app in the Xero App Store.

competitors.name: A2X
competitors.note: Established connector; scout reports 4.96★ from 945 ratings.

rounds.plain: The complaints were aimed at Stripe and Xero themselves, and established connectors already cover reconciliation. The report concluded there was nothing a third party could fix.

risks: The reported complaints concern behavior controlled by Stripe or Xero.
Established connectors already cover reconciliation.

records.summary: This would let businesses export and archive Xero data when leaving Xero or making backups. The sources describe existing export services, but do not give further product details for the proposed tool.
records.customer: Businesses leaving Xero or needing backups
records.paid_demand: The reports name existing one-off paid exports: Boxkite sells an export with attachments for $49, and Xportmydata charges $120. These are listed prices, not verified revenue.

competitors.name: Numerint
competitors.note: Also named as an existing service.

competitors.name: XportMyData
competitors.note: Scout record gives 2.82★ from 11 reviews; listed Oct 2020.

rounds.plain: The market was judged served, with multiple existing export tools and stated one-off prices.

risks: Demand was unmeasured in the scout record.

records.summary: This would be a consumer app for UK smart-meter and home-energy data. The sources do not specify further features for the proposed app.
records.customer: UK consumers with smart meters

competitors.name: Hildebrand Bright
competitors.note: Provides consumers with half-hourly smart-meter data through the DCC.

rounds.plain: Bright is free and provides half-hourly consumer data through the DCC, and n3rgy also has a consumer portal. The report says incumbents have cheaper data access and free apps.

risks: Consumer data access requires a consent-based provider; route and cost were unverified.
Data-access integration may be brittle.
records.moat: Data access is both the potential moat and a blocker; incumbents already have access and free apps.

records.summary: This would replace the stale Tide Times UK app with a UK tide-times app. The sources do not specify additional features for the proposed successor.
records.customer: People looking up UK tide times
records.market: UK; Google Play and Apple App Store

competitors.name: Tides Near Me
competitors.note: Uses UKHO data under the OGL.

competitors.name: Tide Times UK
competitors.note: Scout reports Android 4.0★, 10k+ downloads, last updated 25 Jan 2020.

rounds.plain: The report found the market served by active apps, including My Tide Times. It also flags UKHO data licensing as a consideration.

risks: The market is already served by active apps.
UKHO data licensing cost was unverified.
records.moat: Fails the moat check; active apps already serve the market.

records.summary: This would sell UK-specific digital templates, such as landlord compliance kits, Right to Rent logs, and HMRC or self-assessment trackers. The scout proposed selling them on Gumroad or Etsy.
records.customer: UK landlords and people managing HMRC or self-assessment tasks
records.paid_demand: The reports found little demand evidence: nearly all UK-specific Gumroad search results had 0 ratings. Etsy mass PLR bundles had 600-800 reviews, but were priced at £1.49-£1.65.

rounds.plain: The Gumroad supply was thin but showed no demand signal, while low-priced Etsy bundles could copy a winner. The report found no moat.

risks: Demand for UK-specific templates was unproven.
AI-generated template bundles could copy a winner quickly.
records.moat: None; the report says template winners could be copied within weeks.

records.summary: This would sell fixed-scope spreadsheet, CSV, or n8n workflow automation as a recurring gig. The sources describe it as a service that involves client scoping and communication.
records.customer: Businesses needing recurring spreadsheet or workflow automation
records.paid_demand: Upwork already lists recurring Excel/CSV workflow products at $59-199 tiers. This is listing evidence, not verified revenue.

rounds.plain: The report says client scoping and communication break the 50% automation and 5 h/week limits. The rule-based decision did not depend on further market research.

risks: Client scoping and communication reduce automation.
Hours likely exceed 5 h/week.
The source flags selling to small businesses as a rule to check.
records.moat: Crowded supply; the report identifies narrow vertical focus as the only differentiation and says this is service work, not a product.

records.summary: This would be software for statutory inspections and certificates in a narrow UK trade, such as fire, LOLER lifting, or F-gas. The cited examples manage inspection records and dates for trade businesses.
records.customer: UK trade contractors and inspectors
records.paid_demand: The report says FireCert revenue was Stripe-verified per wlad.me. A LinkedIn post says LolerFlow had 5 companies at £250/mo after 6 months.

competitors.name: FireCert
competitors.note: 39 subscriptions and ~$4,515 MRR per wlad.me, described as Stripe-verified.

competitors.name: LolerFlow
competitors.note: LinkedIn post reports 5 companies after 6 months.

rounds.plain: The report says the buyers are local trade contractors reached through sales, which Ricardo has ruled out. It also flags support and automation constraints.

risks: Buyers are local trade businesses, ruled out in the sources.
Needs sales calls and support.
Automation was estimated at about 50%.
records.moat: Moderate; domain knowledge and standards may provide a moat.

records.summary: This proposed syncing HubSpot invoices and payments to Xero or QuickBooks for UK teams. The scout focused on payment status, fees, and refunds, but the later validation says the premise is wrong.
records.customer: HubSpot users in the UK using Xero or QuickBooks
records.market: UK; HubSpot ecosystem, Xero and QuickBooks
records.paid_demand: The only demand evidence described is one HubSpot Community post, which the scout says had 0 replies and read like vendor research. Existing connectors are named, but the reports do not verify their revenue.

competitors.name: Invoice Stack
competitors.note: Existing connector named in the report.

competitors.name: Inbound Addons Xero
competitors.note: Existing app named in the scout.

competitors.name: Synder
competitors.note: Funded connector named in the report.

rounds.plain: The later re-fetch says the premise is wrong and raised confidence to high. The validation says funded connectors and HubSpot’s native QBO integration already serve the space, while demand evidence is one community post.

risks: The premise was judged wrong in the later re-fetch.
Demand evidence is weak.
Existing connectors already serve the space.
records.moat: Weak; the scout says the market is crowded with funded connectors.

records.summary: This would offer software for filing accounts with Companies House, aimed at dormant and micro companies ahead of the software-only filing requirement. The report says the requirement starts 1 April 2028 and that small and micro companies no longer have to file profit and loss accounts.
records.customer: UK dormant and micro companies
records.paid_demand: The sources list competing filing services at £5, £10+VAT, £19, and £20/yr. These are listed prices, not verified revenue.

rounds.plain: The report says the market is already crowded at £5–£20/yr before the mandate, and filing errors carry liability and support load. It records the filing change as starting 1 April 2028.

risks: Crowded market at a low price floor.
Filing errors create liability and support load.
The software filing mandate starts 1 April 2028.
records.moat: No moat identified; the report describes the tools as cheap commodity products.

records.summary: This would provide maintained successors to popular WordPress.org plugins that have been abandoned, where no maintained alternative exists. The scout cited BackUpWordPress and Heartbeat Control as examples, but validation found maintained alternatives or ongoing support.
records.customer: WordPress site owners using abandoned plugins

competitors.name: WP Media
competitors.note: Report says Heartbeat Control is still supported.

rounds.plain: The report found maintained alternatives for the large orphaned plugins and says support threads cost hours. It also notes third parties publish lists of abandoned plugins.

risks: Large orphaned plugins already have maintained alternatives.
Support threads can take hours.

records.summary: This would add Gift Aid declarations and an HMRC Charities Online export for small charities using WordPress. The scout thought there was no dedicated plugin, but validation found several products covering the work.
records.customer: Small charities using WordPress

competitors.name: Sky Gift Claim
competitors.note: HMRC-listed product that covers Gift Aid.

rounds.plain: The scout’s claim that no dedicated plugin existed was out of date. Validation found multiple products covering Gift Aid declarations or export.

risks: The previously identified gap has closed.
The scout flags small local charities as borderline customers.
records.moat: The scout describes HMRC recognition for direct claims as a barrier and small moat, but validation found several products already serving the need.

records.summary: This would sync Shopify orders with Royal Mail Click & Drop, with a proposed focus on international orders, Northern Ireland, or multiple locations. It was also used as a benchmark for how quickly similar apps can be copied.
records.customer: Shopify merchants using Royal Mail Click & Drop
records.paid_demand: MakePost lists a free plan and a $5.99/mo plan. This is listing evidence; the reports do not verify revenue.

competitors.name: Royal Mail Click & Drop app
competitors.note: Scout reports 1.6★ from 89 ratings; 46 of 75 low reviews concerned sync.

competitors.name: Shopify native Royal Mail labels
competitors.note: Shopify has sold Royal Mail labels natively since Aug 2025, per scout.

rounds.plain: The benchmark was reconfirmed: recent entrants launched in September and October 2026, and an established app already exists. The scout says four apps launched in about five weeks, indicating fast copying.

risks: Four new apps appeared in about five weeks, according to the scout.
Shopify offers Royal Mail labels natively.
records.moat: Fails the moat check; recent entrants appeared quickly.
